title: 8 random letters or 4 random words?
hook: Both are picked at random. One looks far harder to guess. Count before you choose.

knows: multiplying choices (2 shirts x 3 trousers = 6 outfits)
doesNotKnow: how to compare password strength by counting equally likely possibilities

misconception: A long-looking string of random letters is stronger than a few random words.
objective: The learner can compare 26^8 (about 209 billion) with 2048^4 (about 17.6 trillion), say the words win by about 84 times, and explain that each added letter multiplies by 26 and each added word by 2,048.

claims.text: 8 random lowercase letters give 208,827,064,576 possible passwords; 4 random words from a list of 2,048 give 17,592,186,044,416, about 84 times more.
claims.source: Node: 26**8 = 208827064576, 2048**4 = 17592186044416, ratio 84.24. Demo.tsx computes with BigInt (count()).

claims.text: At 10 billion guesses a second, trying every 8-letter password takes about 21 seconds and every 4-word password about 29 minutes.
claims.source: 208827064576 / 1e10 = 20.9 s; 17592186044416 / 1e10 = 1759 s = 29.3 min. The 10-billion rate is a stated assumption on the stage, not a measured attacker speed.

claims.text: Each extra letter multiplies the count by 26, each extra word by 2,048.
claims.source: Multiplication principle: n independent choices from a pool of p give p^n; p^(n+1) = p x p^n.

claims.text: Strength is the number of equally likely passwords, which holds only if every letter or word is picked at random.
claims.source: NIST SP 800-63B (2017), Appendix A: entropy estimates apply to randomly generated secrets; human-chosen passwords are far weaker. Bonneau, 'The science of guessing', IEEE S&P 2012.

claims.text: Live counts on the stage, e.g. 10 letters give 141,167,095,653,376 and 6 words give 73,786,976,294,838,206,464 (try all: about 4 hours and 234 years at 10 billion a second); the bar shows the number of digits.

recall.question: Which has more equally likely possibilities: 3 random words from a 2,048-word list, or 6 random digits (0-9)?
recall.why: 2048^3 = 8,589,934,592 against 10^6 = 1,000,000: each word multiplies by 2,048, each digit only by 10.
